title: Thermos vacuum-gap field-emission access switch
idea: Random stimulus 'thermos flask': its vacuum blocks heat, so a sealed 4-6 nm vacuum gap blocks charge. The access device is a wordline-gated nano-emitter (low-work-function LaB6 or Cs-dosed tip) facing the storage node; off-state current is Fowler-Nordheim-limited to essentially zero, and raising the gate field opens a ~uA emission pulse for read/write.
why: Removes subthreshold, GIDL and junction leakage paths at once (fact 3): retention limited only by capacitor dielectric, refresh interval 100x+ longer, ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy nearly eliminated.

title: Airlock two-gate pillar using stack-effect isolation
idea: Random stimulus 'airlock': two doors that are never open together. Split the vertical access pillar's gate into two independently driven segments (upper/lower wordlines, no added footprint); in retention both are off and the floating mid-channel node self-biases, giving the storage-side segment negative Vgs and near-zero Vds (the stack effect), while both open together within ~1 ns for access.
why: Stack effect cuts subthreshold leakage ~10-30x and suppresses DIBL on the storage side, pulling the <=13 fA tail toward ~1 fA so the refresh interval rises 8x+ (fact 3) at zero footprint cost in a vertical-channel cell.

title: Sourdough-starter replica cells clock each mat's refresh
idea: Random stimulus 'sourdough starter': you feed it when it looks hungry, not on a fixed clock. Each mat holds 64 deliberately weakened replica cells (shorter gate, thinner spacer) written high at every refresh; a comparator fires that mat's refresh only when the median replica sags past threshold, so the interval tracks real temperature, aging and process instead of a worst-case 64 ms at 85 C.
why: Most mats retain for seconds; replica-gated refresh cuts refresh operations and their 16-33% idle-power share by ~70-90% while the deliberately weaker replicas guarantee coverage (fact 3).

title: Turtle-shell back plate that retracts the channel during retention
idea: Random stimulus 'turtle shell': pull in when idle, come out to act. A thin-body access channel sits on a buried per-mat back plate; idle mats drive the plate to -1.5 V, raising Vt ~250 mV (about 3.5 decades of subthreshold current), and an activate command returns the plate to 0 V within ~5 ns through a local driver.
why: Gives retention-time high Vt without paying the on-current penalty of a permanently high-Vt device; subthreshold tail down ~1000x, letting refresh run 10x+ slower (fact 3) and shrinking negative-wordline pumps.

title: Ratchet ferroelectric gate that locks Vt high after every access
idea: Random stimulus 'ratchet wrench': it turns freely one way, then locks. A thin HZO layer in the access gate stack is pulsed to low-Vt polarization at wordline rise, and a short negative tail pulse at wordline fall ratchets it back to a +0.5 V high-Vt state, so retention-state isolation needs no standing negative wordline bias.
why: Decouples on-current from off-leakage (fact 3) and removes negative-wordline pumps from the periphery (fact 7); leakage tail down ~1000x. Risk: needs ~1e15 minor-loop cycles versus HZO's ~1e11-1e12 today.

title: Lighthouse-lit rows: photoconductive wide-gap access channels
idea: Random stimulus 'lighthouse': a beam sweeps, and only what it touches is lit. Each row gets a silicon-nitride waveguide carrying a ~365 nm pulse that photogenerates carriers in GaN access channels beneath it; in the dark a 3.4 eV-gap channel has essentially zero intrinsic carriers, so the bit is isolated with no gate voltage at all.
why: Dark current of a wide-gap photoconductor sits orders of magnitude below 1 fA (fact 3) and the 3 V wordline pump disappears (fact 10). Speculative: photocarrier lifetime must be ns-short and waveguide pitch must reach row pitch.

title: Zipper NEMS contact closes at one volt, opens to air
idea: Random stimulus 'zipper': it closes progressively from one end with little force. A curved nano-cantilever contact anchored at the bitline zips onto the storage-node pad under a ~1 V wordline because the electrostatic gap at the zipping front is tiny; released, it springs back to a 10 nm gap, with Ru/RuO2 contact faces and a hermetic cavity to fight stiction.
why: A physical gap has no subthreshold or junction leakage, so refresh nearly vanishes, and low actuation voltage attacks the 3 V wordline floor (facts 3, 10). Risk: 1e15-cycle contact endurance.

title: Ice-cube-tray GaP storage junction lattice-matched to silicon
idea: Random stimulus 'ice cube tray': each cube sits inside a wall of a different material. Grow the storage-node-side source/drain of the access transistor as epitaxial GaP (2.26 eV gap, within 0.4% of silicon's lattice constant), so the junction where charge leaks has ~1e10x fewer intrinsic carriers and far weaker band-to-band tunneling.
why: Junction generation current scales with n_i and GIDL is band-to-band tunneling at that edge; both collapse in a wide-gap pocket, targeting the 13 fA tail (fact 3) for 10-100x longer retention. Risk: antiphase domains and Ga/P cross-doping into the channel.

title: Gear-shift bitline restore through stepped reservoir rails
idea: Random stimulus 'bicycle gears': climb the hill in small steps instead of one strain. During refresh the sense amp swings bitlines to VARY in four steps via switched on-die reservoir capacitors (0.25/0.5/0.75 VARY) that are recharged by the previous row's discharge, instead of one hard swing from the rail; refresh has timing slack, so the slower adiabatic swing costs no bandwidth.
why: Stepwise charging dissipates ~CV^2/N rather than CV^2/2, so refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) falls ~50-70% without touching the cell.

title: Milk-carton expiry dates let dying data skip refresh
idea: Random stimulus 'milk carton expiry date': some contents are gone before they spoil. The compiler/runtime tags allocations (activations, KV-cache tiles, gradient buffers) with a deadline; a per-row expiry register in the DRAM refresh engine skips refresh for any row whose data is guaranteed overwritten or freed before its retention window ends.
why: In AI training most HBM rows are rewritten within 10-60 ms; skipping them cuts refresh operations 50-80% and recovers much of the 10-20% bandwidth tax (fact 3).

title: Tailor-trimmed access transistors: charge-trap Vt fix for tail cells
idea: Random stimulus 'tailor': alter only the garments that do not fit. Add a thin nitride trap layer to the access gate stack; after retention screening at wafer test, the ~1 ppm leaky cells get a one-time Fowler-Nordheim program pulse that adds ~150 mV of Vt, pulling them back into the main distribution.
why: The refresh interval is set by the worst-ppm tail, not the median; trimming it lets refresh go from 64 to ~512 ms (8x) for all cells (fact 3). Risk: trapped-charge retention over 10 years at 85 C.

title: Toaster-pulse anneals heal retention-tail traps in the field
idea: Random stimulus 'toaster': short hot bursts restore crispness. Embed resistive heater lines in each mat under a deuterium-loaded nitride cap; during maintenance windows a microsecond-scale pulse heats the array locally to ~350 C, releasing deuterium that re-passivates the interface traps behind variable-retention-time cells and aged GIDL tails.
why: Turns the retention tail from a fixed guardband into something repairable; healing aged traps could hold refresh at fresh-die rates and reclaim 2-4x retention margin over life (fact 3).

title: Castle moat liner with negative fixed charge around storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'castle moat': a ring that repels attackers before they reach the wall. Line the isolation trench beside each storage-node junction with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (borrowed from solar-cell field passivation), accumulating holes at the junction periphery and pinching the depletion region where trap-assisted and GIDL leakage live.
why: Periphery traps dominate the leakage tail; field passivation can cut tail leakage 3-10x (fact 3) with one ALD liner and no new masks.

title: Seesaw cell plate lowers storage-node stress during standby
idea: Random stimulus 'seesaw': push one end down and the other end moves too. In idle mats the shared cell plate drops by ~0.3 V, coupling every storage node down with it; '1' nodes then sit lower against the negative wordline and well, cutting GIDL and junction fields, and the plate rises back just before activation.
why: GIDL depends exponentially on the drain-to-gate field; a 0.3 V standby shift can cut tail leakage several-fold and stretch refresh 2-4x (fact 3) using plate drivers that already exist.

title: Lightning-rod p+ electron drains between neighboring active regions
idea: Random stimulus 'lightning rod': give stray charge a better path to ground. Implant a narrow p+ stripe tied to the well under the passing wordline between neighboring active regions; electrons injected by aggressor wordline toggles recombine there before they can drift into the victim's storage node.
why: Attacks the charge-migration component of row hammer (fact 9) and the hammer-induced leakage that shortens retention; aims to raise the flip threshold from ~1k toward 10k+ activations and cut mitigation refreshes.

title: Bubble-wrap void beneath each storage-node junction
idea: Random stimulus 'bubble wrap': air pockets isolate whatever sits on top. Form a silicon-on-nothing cavity (Si/SiGe epi, SiGe removed laterally, top Si sealed by H2 anneal) under the storage-node junction only, so the junction has no bottom area facing the substrate while the channel stays body-tied.
why: Removes bottom-area junction generation leakage and substrate-injected minority carriers (fact 3), aiming at 5-10x lower junction leakage without floating-body effects in the channel.

title: Junkyard-magnet gettering band under every array mat
idea: Random stimulus 'junkyard crane magnet': pull the scrap out before it does damage. Form a carbon-implanted, oxygen-precipitate gettering band 1-2 um below each mat that captures Fe, Cu and Ni atoms which would otherwise sit in junctions as single deep-level traps, the usual root of fA-scale retention-tail outliers.
why: Rare tail cells are often single-defect SRH sites; proximity gettering shrinks the tail population ~10x (fact 3) so refresh can slow for every cell.

title: Mousetrap NbO2 threshold switch in series with storage contact
idea: Random stimulus 'mousetrap': nothing happens until the trigger passes a threshold, then it snaps. Insert a thin NbO2 threshold-switching layer in the storage-node contact; in retention the tiny voltage across it keeps it insulating as a second, non-MOS leakage barrier, while the ~VARY/2 seen during access snaps it conductive in nanoseconds.
why: Stacks a leakage blocker with different physics under the MOS tail, so the two tails do not coincide (fact 3). Risk: NbO2 sub-threshold leakage and threshold variation must stay well below fA, and the read signal must survive the snap.

title: Pressed-flower 2 nm silicon channel widens the bandgap
idea: Random stimulus 'pressed flower': flatten it and its properties change. Thin the vertical access channel to a 2-3 nm sheet by self-limited oxidation and strip, where quantum confinement raises silicon's effective bandgap by ~0.2-0.3 eV and gives near-ideal gate control.
why: A wider effective gap suppresses band-to-band GIDL and generation current exponentially, and swing approaches 60 mV/dec: tail leakage down ~10x (fact 3). Risk: mobility and on-current loss, sheet-thickness variation.

title: Metronome refresh locked to AI all-reduce phases
idea: Random stimulus 'metronome': everything happens on the beat. The accelerator tells HBM the beat of its training step, and the memory controller bunches all refresh into the predictable windows when HBM is idle (network all-reduce, optimizer step on cached data) instead of spreading it uniformly.
why: Hides most of the 10-20% refresh bandwidth tax (fact 3) without changing the cell; needs only system firmware plus a small refresh-postpone extension.

title: Wine-cellar retention bins sell short-retention dies to rewrite-heavy buyers
idea: Random stimulus 'wine cellar': each vintage goes to the buyer it suits. Bin dies by measured retention: long-retention bins (>=1 s) sell at a premium to edge/mobile, while dies failing the 64 ms spec, now scrapped or repaired, ship to AI training racks with a 16 ms controller-managed refresh, where data is rewritten every few ms anyway.
why: Converts retention-yield loss into supply; recovering a few percent of dies at today's 4x prices adds real bits and dollars (cost per bit, usable supply).

title: Retention passport fused into every die, read by hosts
idea: Random stimulus 'passport': a document that travels with you and gets stamped at each border. Propose a JEDEC field in which each die fuses its per-bank retention class and temperature slope at test; the host reads the passport at boot and sets per-bank refresh, instead of every part inheriting the worst-case 64/32 ms spec.
why: Industry-wide policy that turns test data DRAM makers already collect into 2-4x fewer refreshes system-wide (fact 3) with no new silicon.

title: Abacus-bead Coulomb-blockade island isolating the storage node
idea: Random stimulus 'abacus bead': beads move one at a time and only when pushed. Place a sub-2 nm silicon nanodot between the access channel and the storage node; its >0.3 eV charging energy blocks single-electron leakage when the wordline is off, and the wordline lowers the blockade to let charge through.
why: Coulomb blockade gives a non-thermionic off state that does not share the subthreshold tail (fact 3). Speculative: room-temperature blockade needs atomically controlled dot size and must still pass ~1e4 electrons per access.

title: Cactus clean: anhydrous in-situ surface prep for access gates
idea: Random stimulus 'cactus': it thrives on almost no water. Replace the HF-last/SC1/SC2 wet sequences before the access-transistor gate oxide, buried-wordline liner and storage-contact epi with a cluster-tool chain of anhydrous HF/NH3 vapor etch, atomic-hydrogen radical clean and in-situ ALD, with no air break, so no native oxide ever needs a wet strip.
why: The access-device module carries ~20 pre-clean steps at ~20-50 L of UPW per wafer each; dry in-situ prep cuts that module's water >10x and lowers interface-trap density, which also trims the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Snowball CO2 aerosol and supercritical rinse for wordline trenches
idea: Random stimulus 'snowball': a frozen projectile cleans, then disappears. Post-etch particle removal in high-AR buried-wordline trenches and vertical-channel pillars uses cryogenic CO2 snow jets followed by a supercritical-CO2 rinse/dry with a little cosolvent, replacing DI megasonic rinses and IPA drying; the CO2 is recaptured and recycled.
why: Removes DI-rinse and IPA-dry water from the access module (>10x less on those steps) and eliminates capillary collapse of 60:1 structures, a yield loss that falls on leakage-critical pillars.

title: Lego bottom-up ruthenium wordlines with no CMP
idea: Random stimulus 'Lego': pieces snap on only where they belong. Grow the buried wordline by area-selective ALD/CVD of Ru (or Mo) from a seeded trench bottom, with the oxide top surface blocked by a vapor-dosed small-molecule inhibitor, so metal fills bottom-up to the exact recess height: no overburden, CMP, wet recess etch or post-CMP brush clean.
why: Deletes the slurry and post-CMP clean water of the wordline loop (>10x for that module) and removes tungsten (China ~80%); a lower-resistance wordline also allows a lower boosted voltage (fact 10).

title: Fridge-magnet doping: dopant-free charge-plasma access transistor
idea: Random stimulus 'fridge magnet': it holds by field, not glue. Make the array access transistor junctionless and implant-free: low-work-function metal contacts (e.g., Er/Hf silicide) electrostatically induce n-type source/drain in undoped silicon ('charge plasma'), and channel Vt comes from the gate metal work function rather than halo/well implants.
why: Each array implant needs litho, an SPM resist strip and a wet clean; deleting ~6 of them cuts array-FEOL UPW >10x, and with no metallurgical junction there is no junction leakage and the GIDL field is softer (fact 3).

title: Tea-bag vapor monolayer doping grades the storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'tea bag': steep it gently and the dose is set by contact. Dose the storage-node side of the vertical channel with a self-limiting vapor-phase phosphorus-precursor monolayer, cap it in situ and flash-anneal; one dry cycle gives a conformal, deliberately graded, low-peak junction on every pillar face.
why: Replaces angled implants, their resist strips and wet cleans (>10x less water for the junction loop), and the graded profile lowers the peak field that drives GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling: tail leakage 3-5x lower (fact 3).

title: Bonsai pillars: grow vertical channels instead of etching them
idea: Random stimulus 'bonsai': shape the growth rather than carve the wood. Form vertical access channels by selective epitaxy upward from bitline-contact seeds through a patterned oxide template made with one low-AR etch, so there is no 60:1 silicon etch, no etch-polymer wet strip and no damaged sidewall.
why: Deletes the high-AR etch-clean-rinse loop (>10x less water for the pillar module) and yields damage-free channel sidewalls with fewer interface traps, attacking the leakage tail at its source (fact 3).

title: Camel HBM rated to 125 C enables waterless warm cooling
idea: Random stimulus 'camel': built to tolerate heat instead of drinking to stay cool. Rate a hot SKU of HBM to 125 C junction by combining an elevated-Vt array (+150 mV gate work function), base-die refresh that scales with temperature and hot-screened dies, so accelerator coolant loops can run 45-50 C inlet and reject heat through dry coolers all year with no evaporation.
why: HBM's ~85-95 C ceiling often forces cold coolant and evaporative towers; dry cooling takes memory-attributable cooling water from ~1.5-2 L/kWh to near zero, far more than 10x, with the extra leakage at temperature (fact 3) absorbed by design.

title: Thermostat-dial controller trades refresh rate for cooling water hourly
idea: Random stimulus 'thermostat dial': one knob, two costs. The memory controller publishes a live curve of refresh overhead versus HBM temperature; the facility's cooling optimizer runs memory hotter (refresh doubles per ~10 C) during hot afternoons instead of switching cooling towers to evaporative mode, and lets memory cool down on cool nights.
why: Spending a few watts of extra refresh (fact 3) to stay in dry-cooling mode through peak hours avoids most evaporative hours; memory cooling water falls >10x in temperate climates using existing chips.

title: Onion-shell 3D access devices: one etch, one clean, many tiers
idea: Random stimulus 'onion': many layers around one core, peeled at once. In a vertical-bitline 3D DRAM the access transistors of all ~32 tiers are concentric gate-all-around shells around one bitline hole, defined by a single hole etch, one dry clean and one conformal channel/gate deposition, with each tier's wordline a lateral plane.
why: Wet steps per wafer are nearly tier-independent, so water per bit falls ~1/N: 32 tiers gives >10x less water per bit while attacking the missing manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2).

title: Dry-erase resist patterns the array without developer baths
idea: Random stimulus 'dry-erase marker': mark and wipe with no liquid. Pattern the access-device critical layers (active area, buried wordline, storage contact) with vapor-deposited metal-oxide EUV resist that is dry-developed and stripped in plasma, so there is no spin coat, TMAH develop, DI rinse or wet strip.
why: Removes the track's develop/rinse water and the wet strips for the 5-7 array critical layers (>10x less water on those litho loops) and lowers line-edge roughness, which narrows the Vt and leakage spread (facts 3, 4).

title: Gecko-feet dry transfer of 2D access channel sheets
idea: Random stimulus 'gecko feet': stick and release by van der Waals forces, no glue. Grow wafer-scale WSe2/MoS2 on a sapphire donor, pick it up with a dry thermal-release stamp and laminate it onto the BEOL storage-capacitor array, forming the access transistors with ALD gates above the capacitors so the array needs no FEOL silicon access module.
why: Atomically thin, ~2 eV-gap channels give sub-fA off current (fact 3); replacing ~20 FEOL wet loops with one dry transfer plus ALD cuts access-module water >10x, and the sapphire donor is reusable.

title: Hibernating-bear wordlines hold their own negative bias, pumps off
idea: Random stimulus 'hibernating bear': store reserves, then shut the metabolism down. On entering deep idle, each wordline is charged to -1 V and its driver disconnects, so the wordline's own capacitance holds the negative bias like a DRAM cell with a slow top-up every few seconds; negative pumps and bias generators power down while access leakage falls ~1000x.
why: Idle memory energy (refresh plus pumps, 16-33% of idle power, fact 3) falls ~10x, and the water embedded in that electricity (generation plus cooling, ~2 L/kWh) falls by the same 10x.

title: Thimble capacitor: ultra-low leakage lets Cs shrink tenfold
idea: Random stimulus 'thimble': a tiny cup is enough if nothing spills. Pair a sub-0.01 fA access device with local short-bitline sense amps so a 0.5 fF stubby capacitor (AR ~8:1) holds the bit, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar etch, the support-mesh wet removal and the many high-AR cleans and IPA/scCO2 dries of today's capacitor module.
why: The capacitor module is one of DRAM's thirstiest loops; a low-AR capacitor cuts its UPW >10x and breaks the charge wall (fact 1) by needing less charge instead of chasing AR 115.

title: Soap-bubble air-gap spacers made by dry polymer decomposition
idea: Random stimulus 'soap bubble': a film that vanishes and leaves only air. Place a sacrificial polynorbornene spacer between the buried-wordline cap and the storage-node contact; after sealing under a porous cap, a 400 C anneal decomposes it to gas, leaving a k=1 air gap with no wet release and no rinse.
why: The air gap cuts wordline-to-node fringing field (lower GIDL, fact 3) and coupling (row hammer, fact 9); dry decomposition replaces the wet spacer strip/rinse loop (>10x less water for that step).

title: Sandpaper-free planarization by gas-cluster ion beams
idea: Random stimulus 'sandpaper': smoothing without grit. Planarize the array STI fill, wordline cap and landing-pad layers with gas-cluster ion beam (GCIB) location-specific smoothing driven by in-line topography maps, replacing CMP, its slurry and the post-CMP brush/megasonic cleans.
why: CMP plus post-clean is a major UPW and slurry-waste user; dry GCIB on the access module's ~4 planarization steps cuts that water >10x, and damage-free surfaces reduce interface traps (fact 3).

title: Salad-dressing solvent cleans distilled and reused on tool
idea: Random stimulus 'salad dressing': oil and water do not mix, so use the oil. Remove post-etch fluoropolymer residue from wordline and contact etches with hydrofluoroether solvent blends (low surface tension, wets 60:1 trenches without collapse) that are distilled and reused >98% inside the tool, replacing aqueous amine cleans plus DI rinses.
why: Takes aqueous chemistry and rinse water out of the access module's residue cleans (>10x less UPW); low surface tension protects tall pillars and preserves leakage-critical geometry (fact 3).

title: Pendulum resonant wordline drivers recycle 3 V swing energy
idea: Random stimulus 'pendulum': energy swings back and forth instead of being thrown away. During refresh bursts, wordlines are driven as part of an LC resonant tank (integrated inductors on the HBM base die), so each 3 V wordline rise and fall returns most of its charge to the tank instead of burning CV^2 through inefficient pumps.
why: Wordline pumps run at ~30-40% efficiency and the 3 V swing is stuck (fact 10); recovering ~80% of wordline energy cuts the wordline share of refresh energy ~10x, and the generation and cooling water embedded in that energy falls by the same factor.

title: Irrigation-ditch water-rights swap funds dry access-module retrofits
idea: Random stimulus 'irrigation ditch': water is a tradable right, not just a pipe. A DRAM fab in a western U.S. water-rights state retrofits its access-device module to dry cleans and area-selective deposition, then leases the freed allocation to farms or cities under a long-term contract; the water utility co-finances the retrofit because it is cheaper than a new supply source.
why: Turns a 10x water cut in the most clean-heavy module into revenue and a permitting advantage, which speeds new U.S. capacity (U.S. manufacturability, capital intensity).

title: Ration-book liters-per-gigabit ceiling for subsidized DRAM fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'ration book': a fixed allotment forces clever cooking. Tie U.S. memory subsidies to a published liters-per-Gb ceiling for the access-device FEOL that steps down 10x over eight years, with bonus credits for adopting dry clean, dry resist, area-selective deposition and product-level refresh-energy cuts.
why: Creates policy pull for a dry access-module toolset (10x water target) and protects fab siting in water-stressed regions, de-risking U.S. DRAM build-out (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Ice-sculpture cryogenic etch leaves no residue to wash
idea: Random stimulus 'ice sculpture': carved cold, and the shavings sublime away. Etch buried-wordline trenches and vertical channels at about -100 C in SF6/O2 or HF-based plasma, where sidewall passivation is a condensed SiOxFy film that sublimes as the wafer warms, so the post-etch polymer wet strip and its rinses disappear.
why: Removes the wet residue-removal loop after each access-module etch (>10x less water there) and gives smoother, less damaged sidewalls with fewer interface traps (fact 3).

title: Electric-fence gate isolation replaces oxide-filled array STI
idea: Random stimulus 'electric fence': a field keeps the herd apart with no wall. Isolate adjacent access transistors with dedicated always-off isolation-gate lines held at -0.5 V in shallow recesses, in place of deep oxide-filled STI that needs fill, CMP and repeated HF recess dips.
why: Removes the array STI fill-CMP-recess wet loop (>10x less water in that module) and frees area for a wider channel; the isolation gate is placed and biased to shield neighbors rather than hammer them (facts 3, 9).

title: Lawnmower-pattern weight streaming makes inference itself the refresh
idea: Random stimulus 'lawnmower': one planned pass covers the whole lawn. The inference runtime lays out weights so every token's weight sweep visits every HBM row in the refresh counter's order within tREFW; because activation restores the row, the base die verifies the sweep and suppresses explicit refresh for every row it covered.
why: LLM decoding reads all weights every ~20-50 ms, so explicit refresh can drop >90%; refresh energy and its embedded generation and cooling water fall >10x for inference HBM (fact 3).

title: Tear-off notepad: reusable donor wafer for transferred access layers
idea: Random stimulus 'tear-off notepad': many sheets from one block. Form the single-crystal silicon access-transistor layer by repeated hydrogen-split layer transfer from one thick donor wafer (10-20 transfers per donor, plasma touch-up between splits) onto a capacitor-first array wafer, instead of consuming a fresh polished prime wafer as the access substrate.
why: Prime-wafer making (CZ growth in Spruce Pine quartz, slicing, lapping, polishing, cleaning) carries large embedded water; reusing the donor cuts substrate-attributable water per access layer >10x and enables capacitor-first stacking toward 3D (facts 2, 3).
